# Song of Solomon Chapter 1 -- The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1:1** The-Song of-the-Songs [Shir ha-Shirim] which [is] to-Shlomoh.

**1:2** Let-him-kiss-me [yishshaqeni] from-the-kisses of-his-mouth, for your-love [dodekha] [is] better than-wine [mi-yayin]. **1:3** To-the-scent [le-reyach] of-your-oils [shemanekha] good — oil [shemen] poured-out [turaq] [is] your-name [shemekha]; therefore the-young-women [alamot] love-you [ahevukha].

**1:4** Draw-me [mashkheni], after-you let-us-run! The-king has-brought-me to-his-chambers [chadarav]. Let-us-be-glad [nagilah] and-rejoice [venismechah] in-you; let-us-extol [nazkir] your-love more-than-wine. Rightly [mesharim] they-love-you.

**1:5** Dark [shechorah] I [am] and-beautiful [navah], daughters of-Yerushalayim, like-the-tents of-Qedar, like-the-curtains of-Shlomoh. **1:6** Do-not-look-at-me [al tir'uni] that I [am] dark [shecharchoret], that-the-sun has-gazed [shezafatni] upon-me. The-sons of-my-mother were-angry [nicharu] with-me; they-set-me keeper [noterah] of-the-vineyards [ha-kramim]; my-vineyard [karmi] that [is] mine [shelli] I-have-not-kept [lo natharti].

**1:7** Tell-me, [you] whom my-soul [nafshi] loves, where you-graze [tir'eh], where you-make-to-lie-down [tarbitts] at-the-noon [ba-tsohorayim]; for why should-I-be like-one-who-veils-herself [ke-oteyah] beside the-flocks of-your-companions [chavereyikha]?

**1:8** If you-do-not-know, you the-beautiful [ha-yafah] among-women, go-out for-yourself in-the-footsteps [be-iqvei] of-the-flock, and-graze [ur'i] your-kids [gidiyotayikh] beside the-dwellings [mishkenot] of-the-shepherds [ha-ro'im].

**1:9** To-a-mare [le-susati] in-the-chariots [be-rikhvei] of-Pharaoh I-liken-you [dimmitikh], my-companion [ra'yati]. **1:10** Beautiful [are] your-cheeks [lechayayikh] with-ornaments [ba-torim], your-neck [tsavva'rekh] with-strings-of-beads [ba-charuzim]. **1:11** Ornaments of-gold we-will-make for-you with-studs [nekuddot] of-silver.

**1:12** While the-king [was] at-his-table [bi-msibbo], my-nard [nirdi] gave its-fragrance [reycho]. **1:13** A-sachet [tseror] of-myrrh [ha-mor] [is] my-beloved [dodi] to-me; between my-breasts [shadai] he-lies [yalin]. **1:14** A-cluster [eshkol] of-henna [ha-kofer] [is] my-beloved to-me, in-the-vineyards of-Ein-Gedi.

**1:15** Behold, you [are] beautiful [yafah], my-companion; behold, you [are] beautiful; your-eyes [einayikh] [are] doves [yonim]. **1:16** Behold, you [are] beautiful, my-beloved [dodi], indeed pleasant [na'im]; indeed our-bed [arsenu] [is] luxuriant [ra'ananah]. **1:17** The-beams [qorot] of-our-houses [bateynu] [are] cedars [arazim]; our-rafters [rahitenu] [are] cypresses [beroshim].

---

## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1 -- Shir ha-Shirim:** The superlative construction ("song of songs") marks this as the greatest song, parallel to "holy of holies" or "king of kings." The *le-Shlomoh* can mean "by Solomon," "for Solomon," or "about Solomon."

**v.5 -- shechorah ani ve-navah:** The conjunction *ve* can mean "and" or "but." The traditional "black but beautiful" implies a concession; "dark and beautiful" affirms both qualities equally. The Hebrew supports either reading.

**v.9 -- le-susati:** Literally "to my mare." The comparison of a woman to a mare among Pharaoh's chariots is a military-erotic image -- a mare loose among stallions causes chaos. It is a compliment about irresistible attractiveness.

*-- EMET*
